sections.preamble: You answer questions about a single medical image. Follow the answer format requested in the user message exactly.

content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The mass is the large lobulated, heterogeneous structure in the posterior-right part of the image. Its large, relatively homogeneous bright lobe lies at roughly x 120–340 and y 330–610 in the left panel.

The marks that fall in that region are:
- 530, at about (1027, 422) in the right panel, which is about (243, 422) in left-panel coordinates.
- 489, at about (964, 460), which is about (180, 460).
- 458, at about (1027, 524), which is about (243, 524).
- 553, at about (1091, 536), which is about (307, 536).

The large lobe's centre is around (230, 470). Mark 458 at (243, 524) and mark 530 at (243, 422) both sit inside it. Mark 489 at (180, 460) is also inside but closer to the edge.

Taking the whole tumor as the large lobe plus the adjacent lobulated component, the centre would be near (270, 430), which is close to mark 530 at (243, 422). I'll choose 530.

ANSWER: 530
